chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a believing jurist (faqih) dies, a breach occurs in Islam -- a breach that nothing can fill.

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ الْفَقِيهُ: The believing jurist -- one who combines genuine faith (iman) with deep religious understanding (fiqh). This distinguishes mere scholars from those whose learning is grounded in true belief.
key_terms.ثُلْمَةٌ: A crack, breach, or gap -- used metaphorically to describe an irreparable hole in the structure of Islam caused by the loss of a learned believer.

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the death of a learned Muslim scholar?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the irreplaceable importance of a believing scholar who deeply understands the religion (faqih). When such a person dies, a unique void is created in the Muslim community that cannot be compensated by any other means. The hadith was narrated in a context where the Shia community relied heavily on learned scholars to transmit and interpret the teachings of the Imams, making the loss of each such scholar a genuine spiritual and intellectual catastrophe.
